title: Zero-to-POC Canvas + 30/60/90 Facilitation Notes
body:
Purpose:
Run a tightly-scoped customer workshop that produces a validated Zero-to-POC Canvas, draft success criteria, and a concrete 30/60/90 rollout plan. Designed for mid-sized product teams evaluating Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments.

Format options (choose one):
- Rapid (90 minutes): high-level alignment + tech spike plan. Use when customer already has stakeholder alignment but needs a quick validation roadmap.
- Standard (3 hours): full canvas, slide walkthrough, interactive mapping wall, and breakout spike design. Recommended for first full-day engagement.
- Deep Dive (half-day): adds architecture whiteboarding and performance acceptance tests. For technically heavy customers.

Prework (send 4 days ahead):
- Short questionnaire (team, primary use case, expected QPS, latency SLO, data residency constraints).
- Ask for one representative prompt set or a sample conversation flow (for chat use cases) and a small dataset for embedding/retrieval tests.

Agenda (3-hour, standard):
- 0:00–0:10 — Welcome + goals (Facilitator): set expectations; confirm outcomes.
- 0:10–0:30 — Customer context & constraints (Customer leads): product goals, users, privacy/regulatory must-haves. Capture on the canvas.
- 0:30–0:50 — Success Criteria workshop (Group): define 3 measurable success metrics (e.g., 95th p99 latency < 300ms, inference cost <$0.03/token, end-user satisfaction > 4/5). Prioritize.
- 0:50–1:20 — Architecture options & tradeoffs (Facilitator + Eng): hosted vs dedicated vs private; routing/fallback policies; data flow diagram. Use whiteboard.
- 1:20–1:35 — Break (short)
- 1:35–2:05 — Hands-on mapping wall (Interactive): map data sources, privacy touchpoints, and model artifacts to deployment options. Dot-vote risks and unknowns.
- 2:05–2:35 — Experiment design & quick wins (Breakouts): design 2 small validation spikes (one functional correctness, one performance/cost). Document acceptance criteria and estimated effort.
- 2:35–2:50 — 30/60/90 draft plan (Facilitator): align owners and milestones, dependencies, and go/no-go gates.
- 2:50–3:00 — Next steps & commitments (Wrap): agree on deliverables, dates, and communication cadence.

Zero-to-POC Canvas (one-page deliverable — fill during session):
- Use case summary: 1–2 lines.
- Primary personas & business KPIs: list.
- Must-have compliance/controls: list.
- Traffic profile: expected QPS, peak concurrency, avg sequence length.
- Latency & cost targets: hard SLOs and soft targets.
- Recommended deployment mode: hosted | dedicated | private (with rationale).
- Minimal viable model and fallback: model family, quantization/size recommendation, fallback policy.
- Data path & residency: inbound sources, logging, PII handling, retention.
- Success metrics & acceptance criteria (3 items).
- 2 validation spikes (title, owner, success criteria, estimated effort in days).
- 30/60/90 milestones (see below).

Sample slide outline (10–12 slides, short deck to leave with customer):
1) Title + objective (one sentence). Speaker note: what problem we solve together.
2) Agenda & deliverables from today.
3) Customer context snapshot (pulled from prework).
4) Zero-to-POC Canvas (visual one-pager).
5) Deployment tradeoffs (hosted/dedicated/private) — pros/cons table.
6) Measurement & acceptance strategy (latency, cost, quality).
7) Validation spikes (two experiments with owners & timelines).
8) 30/60/90 rollout plan (milestones).
9) Risk register & mitigation (top 5).
10) Operational considerations (observability, rollouts, fallback).
11) Pricing/commitment ask (if applicable).
12) Next steps & owners.

Facilitation notes (tips and micro-scripts):
- Opening: "We’ll leave today with a one-page POC plan and two experiments you can run within 2–4 weeks."
- When getting stuck on scope: use the "no-more-than-3" rule — at most 3 KPIs, 3 stakeholders, 3 technical unknowns for the POC.
- Dot-vote technique: give each participant 3 dots to allocate across risks/unknowns. Use top-3 as spike focus.
- Timeboxing: call out remaining time at 5-minute marks; assign someone as timekeeper.
- Handling disagreements on deployment: refocus on acceptance criteria. Ask "Which deployment lets us test the primary success metric fastest?"

Breakout templates (copy into a doc during workshop):
- Spike title
- Hypothesis (one sentence)
- Data required
- Steps (1–5 bullets)
- Success criteria (explicit measurement)
- Owner & estimate (days)

30/60/90 Example plan (deliverable to leave with customer):
- Day 0–30 (Discovery & fast validation):
  - Finalize POC scope, run spike 1 (functional) and spike 2 (performance), deliver sample outputs.
  - Deliverable: working notebook + perf report (p95/p99, token cost).
  - Owner: Solutions Eng (initial), Customer Eng.
- Day 31–60 (Integration & ops):
  - Integrate model into staging path, add tracing/cost telemetry, run canary with subset of traffic.
  - Deliverable: staging endpoint, alerts, dashboard.
  - Owner: Customer infra + Redwood SRE/Eng.
- Day 61–90 (Scale & handoff):
  - Scale tests to expected QPS, finalize security controls, sign-off on go/no-go gates.
  - Deliverable: runbook, SLA checklist, go-live date recommendation.
  - Owner: Product + Customer Ops.

Acceptance gates (go/no-go):
- Quality gate: model meets baseline precision/recall or user satisfaction target on representative dataset.
- Performance gate: meets latency SLOs at target load with acceptable cost.
- Compliance gate: data handling and encryption meet stated requirements.

Top risks & mitigations (to capture on mapping wall):
- Unknown: sample data incompatibility. Mitigation: sample ingestion spike day 1.
- Unknown: auth/integration complexity (SAML, internal proxies). Mitigation: early security sync and integration checklist.
- Risk: cost overrun on inference. Mitigation: use smaller quantized model for canary + Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Deliverables to produce within 5 business days after workshop:
- Filled Zero-to-POC Canvas (single page).
- Two spike runbooks and owners.
- Draft 30/60/90 with milestones and owners.
- Shared slide deck (10–12 slides) and a short summary email template to reach execs.

Checklist for SE before running the workshop:
- Send prework and collect responses.
- Build a starter canvas and pre-populate known fields.
- Provision a lightweight test harness (notebook + token) to demo quick model outputs.
- Prepare mapping wall materials (virtual Miro board or physical sticky notes).
- Confirm attendees include 1 exec sponsor, 1 engineering lead, 1 product owner, 1 security/infra contact.

Follow-up email skeleton (one-paragraph + attachments):
- Opening line: thank you + one-sentence outcome.
- Attachments: canvas, slides, spike runbooks, 30/60/90 plan.
- Call to action: confirm owners and two-week check-in date.

Notes from recent customer run (lessons learned):
- Customers often under-estimate the cost variance between dev and production traffic patterns — show a cost band example early.
- Early encryption/key management conversations avoid late delays for Private deployments.
- Small, high-confidence spikes build trust faster than large, ambiguous proofs.

Outcomes (intended):
- A signed-off POC scope and timeline.
- Two rapid validation spikes with owners and explicit success metrics.
- A clear 30/60/90 roadmap that ties to business KPIs.

Quick reference (one-liners):
- If asked about latency vs cost: "We trade latency for cost via batching/quantization and routing policies — measure both on your sample workload."
- If asked about model drift: "Schedule a quality regression checkpoint in the 60-day milestone tied to production prompts."

End of document.
